results.title: Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine | ResStock

item.text:
**Yes. ResStock has a documented, unresolved problem with Maine’s “Geometry Wall Type” data**, caused by mislabeled county tax assessor records. For example, the 2024 Release 2 data show Maine’s single-family detached homes as roughly 10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete block—an implausible distribution confirmed by local researchers. The team believes all published ResStock datasets are affected. [Official issue report](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The ResStock team recommends:

- **For wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use nearby states as proxies, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**.
- **For upgrade results where eligibility depends on wall type:** reweight Maine results using nearby states’ wall type distributions, or use those states’ results directly. This matters for measures such as insulation upgrades restricted to wood-frame walls. [Recommended workarounds](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)

The team currently does **not** expect significant effects on baseline energy consumption, emissions, or bills, but its investigation remains incomplete. [Impact assessment](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html)
